title: Noor and the Colony
premise: Emrys Sandoval tends the Verdance, a terraformed garden on colony world Kestrel's Landing, and keeps alive a beacon whose original purpose has been forgotten. When she discovers her own name on the manifest of the Halcyon, a colony ship that never launched, she learns the beacon is a message-lock: it will transmit a peace accord to the warring fleet in orbit only when opened by someone listed on that manifest. As factions on both sides race to seize or destroy the beacon before the jump window closes, Emrys must choose between delivering the message — which exposes her family's role in starting the war — and protecting the man she loves, who serves the faction that benefits from silence. She delivers it; the truth ends the war but costs her the garden, her standing, and nearly her life, and she leaves with the fleet as the first citizen of a peace she authored.
about_author: Odile Thackeray is a former botanist who spent six years cataloguing seed vaults in the Andes before turning to fiction full-time. Her stories about inheritance and impossible gardens have appeared in several genre magazines under other names; this is her first novel.

chapters.title: The Garden for No One
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Emrys tends the Verdance alone, recording growth logs for colonists who may never come, and maintains the ancient beacon as a rote duty. A supply drop brings news of escalating orbital hostilities between the Charter fleet and the Breakaway flotilla. Emotional beat: quiet devotion shadowed by loneliness.

chapters.title: A Name That Never Flew
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Auditing old manifests during a dust storm, Emrys finds 'E. Sandoval' aboard the Halcyon — a ship destroyed before launch, decades before her birth. The beacon responds to her touch for the first time, projecting a partial star chart. Emotional beat: uncanny recognition, the thrill of being chosen by something forgotten.

chapters.title: The Man from Orbit
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. A Charter envoy, Captain Idris Vane, descends under truce flag seeking the beacon's origin. He is courteous, weary, and dangerously curious about her discovery. They share dinner among the greenhouses; attraction sparks against mutual suspicion. Emotional beat: warmth blooming in hostile soil.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Buried
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. In the colony archive Emrys finds her grandmother's sealed testimony: the Sandovals helped falsify the Halcyon disaster to hide an atrocity that ignited the war. The beacon holds the proof. Emotional beat: grief curdling into dread — her inheritance is complicity.

chapters.title: Truce at Gunpoint
chapters.summary: POV Idris. A Breakaway strike team lands to seize the beacon; Idris shields Emrys under the collapsing truce. Forced together in the deep tunnels beneath the garden, they negotiate uneasy alliance while gunfire echoes above. Emotional beat: trust forged under fire, desire sharpened by danger.

chapters.title: The Window Closes In
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Decrypted beacon data reveals the jump window — the only alignment allowing fleet-wide transmission — closes in nine days. Both fleets learn of the beacon's existence; bounty notices name Emrys. Idris admits his orders are to destroy it if he can't control it. Emotional beat: ticking-clock panic, love and duty openly at odds.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Greenhouse
chapters.summary: POV Idris. Ordered to extract the beacon core, Idris instead warns Emrys — then is caught by his own executive officer, who broadcasts his treachery and takes the core. The Verdance burns in the assault. Emotional beat: heartbreak and sacrifice; love chosen over duty, and punished for it.

chapters.title: Ashes and Coordinates
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Wounded, Emrys recovers the core from the wrecked garden using knowledge only its keeper has — the living root-network itself carries a backup key. She broadcasts her grandmother's confession planet-wide, forcing both fleets to listen. Emotional beat: fury transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Message
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. At the beacon spire, with the jump window minutes from closing and both fleets targeting her position, Emrys opens the lock with her manifest name and transmits the accord — truth, apology, terms. Fleets hold fire mid-volley. Emotional beat: terrible stillness, then the first breath of peace.

chapters.title: First Citizen of the Quiet
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Weeks later, the ceasefire holds; courts convene over the Halcyon crime, sparing the Sandoval line nothing. Idris, stripped of command, chooses exile beside her. Emrys plants the first seeds of a new garden on neutral ground. Emotional beat: mourning braided with hope — an ending that is also a planting.
